Buzz Aldrin. Born in nineteen thirty, he is an American former astronaut and engineer who was the second person to walk on the Moon during Apollo eleven on July twenty-first, nineteen sixty-nine, nineteen minutes after Neil Armstrong. Serving as the Lunar Module pilot, Aldrin performed experiments, collected samples, and spent two hours and thirty-one minutes on the lunar surface. He represents the culmination of the Cold War space race and remains a prominent advocate for continued lunar and Mars exploration.

Born Edwin Eugene Aldrin Junior in Glen Ridge, New Jersey, he adopted the nickname Buzz as a child. Aldrin earned a doctorate in astronautics from MIT with a thesis on orbital rendezvous techniques crucial to Apollo missions. He conducted seven spacewalks on Gemini twelve in nineteen sixty-six, advancing techniques for extravehicular activity and rendezvous maneuvering. On the Moon, Aldrin deployed the Solar Wind Collector, collected twenty-two kilograms of lunar samples, and took the famous photograph of Armstrong on the lunar surface.

He famously described the lunar landscape as magnificent desolation, capturing both the stark beauty and scientific import of the Moon. After returning from Apollo eleven, Aldrin experienced psychological depression and became a vocal advocate for mental health awareness among astronauts. He continued advocating for space exploration into his nineties, promoting a vision of sustainable lunar bases and Mars missions for future generations. Aldrin developed cycling trajectories for efficient Mars transit, contributing innovative orbital mechanics concepts to spaceflight planning.

These achievements connect him to Neil Armstrong as the spacecraft commander and first person on the Moon, to Apollo eleven as the mission where he achieved his historic landing, to the Apollo program that enabled both his Gemini training and Apollo mission, to the space race as the geopolitical competition driving his selection, and to NASA as the organization employing him throughout his astronaut career.
